operating_notes.text: Supreme Infrastructure has an outstanding claim of ₹45.47 Cr against MMRDA for flyover works at Rajnoli and Mankoli Junctions on NH-3.
NCLT Mumbai Bench granted a 30-day extension for making the balance payment under the approved debt resolution scheme.
SEBI issued observation letter dated May 25, 2026 requiring acquirers to proceed with open offer for 26% voting share capital.
Corporate guarantee exposure for Kopargaon Ahmednagar Tollways (Phase I) Private Limited reduced from ~₹180 Cr to ₹36.51 Cr under a court-approved resolution plan.
FY25-26 Annual Report highlights trade receivables of ₹75,644.24 lakhs under audit qualification for lack of ECL provisioning.
NCLT Mumbai granted extension up to October 31, 2026 for Scheme of Compromise obligations and approved escrow fund release mechanism.

timeline.summary: MMRDA constituted a Dispute Resolution Committee to adjudicate Supreme Infra's ₹45.47 Cr legacy claim for NH-3 flyover works.
Supreme Infrastructure submitted its initial disclosure confirming it is not a Large Corporate for FY 2025-26.
NCLT Mumbai Bench granted Supreme Infrastructure a 30-day extension to complete balance payments under its approved debt resolution scheme.
Vikram Sharma, promoter of Supreme Infrastructure India Limited, confirmed no new encumbrance on equity shares held during FY2025-26 as of April 4, 2026.
Systematix Corporate Services informed exchanges that SEBI issued observations for Supreme Infrastructure's open offer, but funding uncertainty persists.
Supreme Infra clarified that SEBI issued observations requiring acquirers to proceed with an open offer for 26% equity shares.
Q1FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹24.12 Cr; net loss ₹59.17 Cr (against a loss of ₹399.92 Cr a year earlier).
Supreme Infrastructure reduced its corporate guarantee exposure from ₹180 Cr to ₹36.51 Cr via a court-approved resolution plan for Kopargaon Ahmednagar Tollways.
Supreme Infrastructure appointed former Chief Commissioner of Income Tax Dr. Prabhakant as an Additional Non-Executive Independent Director.
Supreme Infrastructure announced its 43rd AGM for November 12, 2026, alongside the release of its FY25-26 Annual Report containing qualified audit opinions.
NCLT Mumbai Bench granted Supreme Infra an extension until October 31, 2026 to complete payment obligations under its Scheme of Compromise.
